bio: Professor at Universidade Estadual do Tocantins, where she leads the Research Group on Development and Environmental Performance. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, a Master’s degree in Agroecosystems, and a Ph.D. in Regional Development. She has been a Visiting Researcher at the Institute of Management and Strategy, University of St. Gallen, Switzerland. She has provided consultancy to the Ministry of the Environment of Brazil and the Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture. She is a board member of the State Council for Water Resources in Brazil, Ambassador of the Climate Solutions Simulator of MIT, and board member of Metaphorum and the American Society for Cybernetics. Her work focuses on applying the Viable System Model (VSM) to complex adaptive systems, particularly in water governance.

CEO of The Infinite Game and systems thinker with a background in telecommunications, control systems engineering, and organizational design. Former Chief Research Scientist at BT and Project Supervisor at the University of Cambridge and the University of Oxford. Senior Researcher at Khalifa University and Lecturer at the University of Northumbria. Developer of the Ibex Identity Model and frameworks integrating surprise metabolism, recursive closure, and cybernetic stewardship. Chartered Engineer (CEng) and Honorary Fellow of The Cybernetics Society.

affiliation: University of Exeter / De Montfort University
bio: Honorary Senior Lecturer at the University of Exeter and Programme Director at De Montfort University (Cambodia). Consultant and researcher in complexity in management, with previous roles at Leeds Beckett University and Cranfield University. His work focuses on complexity management in strategy, security, sustainability, innovation, and management systems inspired by co-evolving and transition management principles. He has led projects across the UK, Europe, Latin America, and Cambodia.

affiliation: Al Ain University, United Arab Emirates
bio: Associate Professor of Management and Deputy Dean of the College of Business at Al Ain University, UAE. She holds a PhD in Management from the University of Hull, UK. With over a decade of experience in the UAE and Oman, her work focuses on sustainability, leadership, entrepreneurship, and workforce psychology. She contributes to UN-PRME Youth Talks and the PRME Mentorship Program, aligning her teaching with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Director of Metaphorum and organizational cybernetics scholar. She earned her PhD in organizational cybernetics in 1995 and worked closely with Stafford Beer. Former Reader in Cybernetics at Hull University Business School and currently an Emeritus Fellow. Honorary Research Fellow at Exeter University and Transylvania Executive Education. Recipient of the Ashby Lecture (2002) and Norbert Wiener Award (2006). Author of books including 'A Complexity Approach to Sustainability' and 'Sustainable Self-governance in Businesses and Societies: The Viable System Model in Action'.

Director at Metaphorum with over forty years of experience in the cooperative business sector. He has established and co-managed multiple businesses and pioneered the use of the Viable System Model in cooperatives and eco-communities. Co-author of 'A Complexity Approach to Sustainability' with Angela Espinosa. He works with the Transition Network, the Permaculture Association, and the Cooperative Group, and consults internationally on complexity and cybernetics.

Lecturer in Management Studies and Operational Disaster Management at the University of Manchester. He holds a PhD in Business and Management (Operations Management) from Alliance Manchester Business School and an MSc from the University of Warwick. His research focuses on enhancing resilience, agility, and viability of systems during emergencies, particularly managing spontaneous volunteers in disasters, using VSM, SSM, and systems thinking methodologies.

Principal at Cwarel Isaf Institute and independent consultant based in Toronto. She worked with Stafford Beer from the early 1980s until his death in 2002. Former President of Metaphorum, the American Society for Cybernetics, and the International Society for Systems Science. She applies cybernetic approaches including the Viable System Model, Team Syntegrity, and Operations Room design in nonprofit and business organizations.

Professor at the University of Valladolid specializing in system dynamics and organizational cybernetics. Creator of the VSMod® software supporting the Viable System Model. Former Director of International Relations at the University of Valladolid (2000–2006). Author of over 80 publications and five books, including 'Design and Diagnosis for Sustainable Organizations: The Viable System Method'. Recipient of the Kybernetes Research Award (2006) and Honorary HSSS Award as Distinguished Scientist (2007). Board member of the World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics and Fellow of HSSS.

Constantin leads the Malik Group in Switzerland as co-owner and co-CEO, where he helps organizations with some of society's most complex challenges—from climate adaptation and public health transformation to reimagining how governments can serve their citizens more effectively. For 20 years, he has worked alongside cities, research institutions, and international corporations to design systems that are resilient, equitable, and capable of evolving with our rapidly changing world. His approach draws on cybernetics and systems science to help leaders see beyond immediate crises and build capacity for long-term transformation. Constantin's academic background spans law, psychology, and business sustainability management. He is a member of the International Society for the Systems Sciences and the American Society for Cybernetics. His book, Ahead of Change, explores how crowd psychology and cybernetics might transform democratic decision-making—offering a glimpse of more adaptive governance for the 21st century. He believes the solutions to our greatest challenges emerge not from single interventions, but from understanding and reshaping the systems that shape our lives.

Germán A. Bula Ph.D. is an attorney (Universidad del Rosario - Colombia). He holds a doctorate and master's degree in Ethics and Democracy from the University of Valencia (Spain), in addition to master’s degrees in economics (National University of Colombia) and in Political Science (IAEE - Madrid). His research lines focus on truth studies and peacebuilding, as well as organizational cybernetics applied to law and public administration. He serves as an arbitrator at the Arbitration Centers of the Chambers of Commerce of Bogotá, Barranquilla, Cartagena, and Pereira. Within the Council of State of Colombia, he has held the positions of President, Magistrate of the Consultation and Civil Service Chamber, and Ad Hoc Justice of the Council of State. He has served as Minister of Education, as well as Deputy Comptroller General of the Republic of Colombia, Ambassador to Venezuela, and Director of the World Center for Research and Training in Conflict Resolution. He is an active member of WOSC, the World   Organization   for Systems and Cybernetics, the Colombian Academy of Jurisprudence, the Ibero-American Forum of Administrative Law (FIDA), and the Franco-Colombian Association of Jurists (AJFC). He is the author of some books and papers. He serves   as   a   reviewer   for   international   journals.  During his professional career he was a professor at several universities, an international lecturer, an organizational consultant, and a litigator. Mail address: consultoresgbe@gmail.com ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6744-2362

John, a practising consultant cybernetician since 1990 is also an experienced Board Chair and Non-Executive Director with a focus on developing strategic and operational adaptation and transformation rooted in cybernetic reasoning. His approach seeks to enhance performance through new insights and thoughtful innovation, working especially with organisations facing challenges of adaptation, survival and growth. Leadership built on effective mentoring enables his coherent whole system approach synthesising the three dimensions of people, process and information. John’s experience extends across public, private and 3rd sector and includes infrastructure, energy, transport, housing, criminal justice, social care, health care and both service focused and manufacturing organisations. John is currently partner in Beckford Consulting, Chair of Corehaus Ltd (MMC housing), Visiting Professor at University College London (Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering) and at Loughborough University Business School (Centre for Information Management). Until April 2025, he was Board Chair at Rise Mutual CIC (Domestic Abuse, VAWG) and NED at Fusion21 Ltd. (2014-2023) Currently co-supervising 3 doctoral students researching data driven decision making and 3 doctoral students researching long term effectiveness of interventions with perpetrators of domestic abuse/VAWG. John holds a PhD in Management Systems and Sciences (Hull), is a Fellow of the Cybernetics Society, a Member of The Institute of Management Services, a Fellow of the Royal Society for the Arts and a Fellow of the Institute of Engineering and Technology. John is immediate Past President of the Cybernetics Society.

Markus Schwaninger is a Professor Emeritus at the Institute of Management and Strategy, University of St. Gallen (Switzerland). Research focus: Organizational intelligence, corporate transformation and learning, systemic issues of sustainability. Methodological orientation: Systems approaches; emphasis: Organizational Cybernetics (Viable Systems, Variety Engineering), System Dynamics.  Studies in Economics, Sociology and Management at Universities in Austria (Salzburg, Innsbruck), Switzerland (St. Gallen) and France (Aix-Marseille). Habilitation and venia legendi at the University of St. Gallen, Switzerland (UNISG). Memberships: WOSC-World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics (advisory board), International Academy of Cybernetics and Systems, System Dynamics Society, ISSS-International Society for the Systems Sciences, GWS-Gesellschaft für Wirtschafts- und Sozialkybernetik, BSSS-Bertalanffy Center for the Study of Systems Science (Fellow). Markus has researched, lectured and consulted internationally. Research residencies abroad: MIT-Massachusetts Institute of Technology, U.S.A.; Columbia University, U.S.A.; UBC-University of British Columbia, Canada; Fundação Getúlio Vargas, Brazil; Universidad de los Andes, Colombia; Instituto Tecnológico da Aeronáutica, Brazil. Founder of the System Dynamics Group at the Institute of Management and Strategy, UNISG. Publishing: Long-standing Managing Editor of the System Dynamics Review. His publications amount to roughly 250, in six languages, including 15 books.

affiliation: World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics
bio: Raúl Espejo is President of the World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics (WOSC) and Director of Syncho Research, UK. He is an academician of the International Academy for Systems and Cybernetic Sciences (IASCYS) and Past Professor of Systems and Cybernetics at the University of Lincoln, UK. His research is in organisational cybernetics and systems. His most referred book is “Organizational Systems: Managing Complexity with the Viable System Model”, 2011 in English and 2016 in Spanish (both with A. Reyes). Has co-published five books and edited 7 special issues of journals, most significantly in 2018 “Futures of Society: the interactions revolution” in Futures. Has published over a 120 papers in journals and books. Has organised and co-organised four of WOSC’s  World Congresses, with Alfonso Reyes in the University of Ibague, Colombia, in 2014, with Sergio Barile in La Sapienza University of Rome, Italy, in 2017, with Vladimir Lepskiy of the Russian Academy of Sciences and Igor Perko, Maribor University Slovenia, virtually from Moscow in 2021, with Igor Perko in the University of Oxford, England in 2023.  In June 2024 he was awarded by the American Society of Cybernetics the Norbert Wiener medal. From 1971 to 1973 he was operations director of the CYBERSYN project - for the Chilean Government aimed at managing the country’s industrial economy, under the scientific direction of Professor Stafford Beer.

A nomad, having previously lived a variety of lifes as a practitioner and academic. Currently at Centre for Systems Engineering in Department of Space and Climate Physics (MSSL) at University College London.  Practitioner experience spans the coal, oil, electronics and tourism industries, in roles that have included manager, director and consultant. Expertise lies in managing organisational transformation (e.g. business recovery, strategic positioning, technology implementation). Awarded a PhD in 2010 from the University of Edinburgh Business School for developing a conceptual explanation (‘domestication’) for how people take up and use online technologies. This has provided a platform to develop a research portfolio that operates at the intersection of technology, sustainability and social complexity. This work is grounded in the conceptual insights of Cybersystemics. and the Sociology of Technology. Stephen’s growing portfolio of publications includes a book, journal, conference and working papers, online journalist articles and evidence to UK Parliament.

Space entrepreneur and PhD candidate in Space Sciences and Technologies at the Aeronautics Institute of Technology (ITA) in Brazil, currently a Visiting Researcher at the Politecnico di Milano (PoliMi). His doctoral research examines the dynamic governance of emerging space ecosystems by integrating Stafford Beer’s Viable System Model (VSM) with organizational process philosophy, shifting the traditional analytical focus from static structures to the emergence of dynamic networks.

Michael C. Jackson is Emeritus Professor at the University of Hull and MD of Systems Research Ltd. He graduated from Oxford University, gained an MA from Lancaster University and a PhD from Hull, and has worked in the civil service, in academia and as a consultant. Between 1999 and 2011, Mike was Dean of Hull University Business School, leading it to triple-crown accreditation. Mike has been President of the International Federation for Systems Research and the International Society for the Systems Sciences. He was editor-in-chief of Systems Research and Behavioral Science for 26 years. In 2011 Mike was awarded an OBE for services to higher education and business. In 2017 he received the Beale Medal of the UK Operational Research Society for ‘a sustained contribution over many years to the theory, practice, and philosophy of Operational Research’. In 2022 he received the Pioneer Award of the International Council on Systems Engineering for ‘the development of the foundations of systems engineering as author, educator and intellectual leader in systems thinking’. Mike is known as a key figure in the development of ‘critical systems thinking’ - a topic on which he has published ten books and over 150 articles. His latest book Critical Systems Thinking: A Practitioner’s Guide was published by Wiley in 2024.

Researcher, consultant, and university professor with over 25 years of experience in applied market research, innovation management, and strategic analysis across diverse economic sectors. Founder and Director of ConCriterio — a marketing innovation think lab supporting markets transformation, sustainability, and mission-oriented innovation processes. My work integrates rigorous mixed-method approaches — deep qualitative inquiry, social network analysis, bibliometrics, systems modeling, spatial analysis, and data science — to understand markets as complex socio-technical systems. I translate empirical and scientific evidence into strategic decisions, contributing to sustainable market formation, transformative innovation, and alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Currently a PhD Candidate in Technology and Innovation Management (UPB, EAFIT scholarship), with a thesis focused on transformative exchange for socio-technical system transitions.
